passages.text: “Here is My Servant, whom I uphold, My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His Servant.
God upholds His Servant.
God has chosen this Servant.
God delights in His Servant.
God puts His Spirit on His Servant.
This Servant will bring justice to the nations.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ אֶתְמָךְ־ בּ֔וֹ בְּחִירִ֖י רָצְתָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י נָתַ֤תִּי רוּחִי֙ עָלָ֔יו מִשְׁפָּ֖ט לַגּוֹיִ֥ם יוֹצִֽיא׃

passages.text: He will not cry out or raise His voice, nor make His voice heard in the streets.
passages.sermon:
God describes His Servant.
God upholds His Servant.
God chooses His Servant.
God delights in His Servant.
God puts His Spirit on His Servant.
The Servant will not cry out.
The Servant will not raise His voice.
The Servant will not make His voice heard in the streets.
passages.original: לֹ֥א יִצְעַ֖ק וְלֹ֣א יִשָּׂ֑א וְלֹֽא־ יַשְׁמִ֥יעַ בַּח֖וּץ קוֹלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish; He will faithfully bring forth justice.
passages.sermon:
God chose His Servant.
God delights in His Servant.
God put His Spirit on His Servant.
God’s Servant acts with gentleness.
He will not break a bruised reed.
He will not put out a smoldering wick.
He will bring justice.
He will do this faithfully.
passages.original: קָנֶ֤ה רָצוּץ֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁבּ֔וֹר וּפִשְׁתָּ֥ה כֵהָ֖ה לֹ֣א יְכַבֶּ֑נָּה לֶאֱמֶ֖ת יוֹצִ֥יא מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: He will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth. In His law the islands will put their hope.”
passages.sermon:
God chose His servant.
God’s servant will not grow weak.
God’s servant will not become discouraged.
God’s servant will continue His work.
He will do this until He establishes justice on the earth.
People in distant lands will hope in His law.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יִכְהֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א יָר֔וּץ עַד־ יָשִׂ֥ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּלְתוֹרָת֖וֹ אִיִּ֥ים יְיַחֵֽילוּ׃פ

passages.text: This is what God the LORD says— He who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and its offspring, who gives breath to the people on it and life to those who walk in it: “I, the LORD, have called you for a righteous purpose, and I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and appoint you to be a covenant for the people and a light to the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon and those sitting in darkness out from the prison house.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God created the heavens.
God stretched out the heavens.
God spread out the earth.
God made everything that comes from the earth.
God gives breath to the people on the earth.
God gives life to all who walk on the earth.
God says, “I am the LORD.
I have called you for a righteous purpose.
I will take hold of your hand.
I will keep you safe.
I will appoint you to be a covenant for the people.
I will make you a light for the nations.
You will open the eyes of the blind.
You will bring prisoners out of the dungeon.
You will bring out those who sit in darkness from the prison house.”
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל׀ יְהוָ֗ה בּוֹרֵ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְנ֣וֹטֵיהֶ֔ם רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ וְצֶאֱצָאֶ֑יהָ נֹתֵ֤ן נְשָׁמָה֙ לָעָ֣ם עָלֶ֔יהָ וְר֖וּחַ לַהֹלְכִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃ אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה קְרָאתִ֥יךָֽ בְצֶ֖דֶק וְאַחְזֵ֣ק בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְאֶצָּרְךָ֗ וְאֶתֶּנְךָ֛ לִבְרִ֥ית עָ֖ם לְא֥וֹר גּוֹיִֽם׃ לִפְקֹ֖חַ עֵינַ֣יִם עִוְר֑וֹת לְהוֹצִ֤יא מִמַּסְגֵּר֙ אַסִּ֔יר מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּ֖לֶא יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

passages.text: I am the LORD; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
His name is the LORD.
He will not give His glory to anyone else.
He will not give His praise to idols.
passages.original: אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא שְׁמִ֑י וּכְבוֹדִי֙ לְאַחֵ֣ר לֹֽא־ אֶתֵּ֔ן וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י לַפְּסִילִֽים׃

passages.text: Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things. Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you.”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God speaks now.
God says, “Look.
The things that happened before have already come.
I now tell you about new things.
I announce these new things before they appear.
I tell you about them before they happen.”
passages.original: הָרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת הִנֵּה־ בָ֑אוּ וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד בְּטֶ֥רֶם תִּצְמַ֖חְנָה אַשְׁמִ֥יע אֶתְכֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Sing to the LORD a new song— His praise from the ends of the earth— you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you islands, and all who dwell in them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
He alone deserves praise.
Sing a new song to the LORD.
Praise Him from every place on earth.
You who travel on the sea, praise Him.
Everything in the sea, praise Him.
People on the islands, praise Him.
Everyone living on the islands, praise Him.
passages.original: שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ יוֹרְדֵ֤י הַיָּם֙ וּמְלֹא֔וֹ אִיִּ֖ים וְיֹשְׁבֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Let the desert and its cities raise their voices; let the villages of Kedar cry aloud. Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them cry out from the mountaintops.
passages.sermon:
The desert and its cities will raise their voices.
The villages where Kedar lives will cry aloud.
The people who live in Sela will sing for joy.
They will cry out from the tops of the mountains.
passages.original: יִשְׂא֤וּ מִדְבָּר֙ וְעָרָ֔יו חֲצֵרִ֖ים תֵּשֵׁ֣ב קֵדָ֑ר יָרֹ֙נּוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי סֶ֔לַע מֵרֹ֥אשׁ הָרִ֖ים יִצְוָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: Let them give glory to the LORD and declare His praise in the islands.
passages.sermon: The people must give glory to the LORD.\r\nThey must speak of His praise in the islands.
passages.original: יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לַֽיהוָ֖ה כָּב֑וֹד וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ׃

passages.text: The LORD goes forth like a mighty one; He stirs up His zeal like a warrior. He shouts; yes, He roars in triumph over His enemies: “I have kept silent from ages past; I have remained quiet and restrained. But now I will groan like a woman in labor; I will at once gasp and pant.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is strong and mighty.
He acts like a powerful warrior.
He stirs up His zeal like a man ready for battle.
He shouts loudly.
He roars over His enemies.
He wins against those who oppose Him.
He says, “I have kept silent for a long time.
I have been quiet and held back.
But now I will cry out like a woman in labor.
I will gasp and pant all at once.”
passages.original: יְהוָה֙ כַּגִּבּ֣וֹר יֵצֵ֔א כְּאִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמ֖וֹת יָעִ֣יר קִנְאָ֑ה יָרִ֙יעַ֙ אַף־ יַצְרִ֔יחַ עַל־ אֹיְבָ֖יו יִתְגַּבָּֽר׃ס הֶחֱשֵׁ֙יתִי֙ מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם אַחֲרִ֖ישׁ אֶתְאַפָּ֑ק כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֣ה אֶפְעֶ֔ה אֶשֹּׁ֥ם וְאֶשְׁאַ֖ף יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn the rivers into dry land and drain the marshes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with power and authority.
The LORD says, “I will destroy the mountains.
I will destroy the hills.
I will make all their plants wither.
I will turn the rivers into dry land.
I will dry up the marshes.”
passages.original: אַחֲרִ֤יב הָרִים֙ וּגְבָע֔וֹת וְכָל־ עֶשְׂבָּ֖ם אוֹבִ֑ישׁ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י נְהָרוֹת֙ לָֽאִיִּ֔ים וַאֲגַמִּ֖ים אוֹבִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: I will lead the blind by a way they did not know; I will guide them on unfamiliar paths. I will turn darkness into light before them and rough places into level ground. These things I will do for them, and I will not forsake them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the speaker.
The LORD acts with power and care.
The LORD leads blind people.
The blind do not know the way.
The LORD guides them on paths they have never walked.
The LORD turns darkness in front of them into light.
The LORD makes rough places smooth and level for them.
The LORD does these things for the blind.
The LORD does not abandon them.
passages.original: וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים בְּדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ בִּנְתִיב֥וֹת לֹֽא־ יָדְע֖וּ אַדְרִיכֵ֑ם אָשִׂים֩ מַחְשָׁ֨ךְ לִפְנֵיהֶ֜ם לָא֗וֹר וּמַֽעֲקַשִּׁים֙ לְמִישׁ֔וֹר אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים עֲשִׂיתִ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתִּֽים׃

passages.text: But those who trust in idols and say to molten images, ‘You are our gods!’ will be turned back in utter shame.
passages.sermon:
Some people trust in idols.
Some people say to molten images, "You are our gods."
God will turn these people back.
God will cover them with utter shame.
passages.original: נָסֹ֤גוּ אָחוֹר֙ יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ בֹ֔שֶׁת הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑סֶל הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לְמַסֵּכָ֖ה אַתֶּ֥ם אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Listen, you deaf ones; look, you blind ones, that you may see!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to people who are deaf and blind.
God commands the deaf to listen.
God commands the blind to look.
God wants the blind to see.
passages.original: הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like the messenger I am sending? Who is blind like My covenant partner, or blind like the servant of the LORD?
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His servant.
God calls His servant blind.
God says, "No one is as blind as My servant."
God calls His messenger deaf.
God says, "No one is as deaf as the messenger I send."
God calls His covenant partner blind.
God says, "No one is as blind as the servant of the LORD."
passages.original: מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּ֣י אִם־ עַבְדִּ֔י וְחֵרֵ֖שׁ כְּמַלְאָכִ֣י אֶשְׁלָ֑ח מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּמְשֻׁלָּ֔ם וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Though your ears are open, you do not hear.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His servant Israel.
You see many things.
You do not pay attention.
Your ears are open.
You do not listen.
passages.original: רָאִיתָ רַבּ֖וֹת וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמֹ֑ר פָּק֥וֹחַ אָזְנַ֖יִם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽע׃

passages.text: The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify His law and make it glorious.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is righteous.
The LORD desires what is right.
The LORD acts for the sake of His righteousness.
The LORD chooses to make His law great.
The LORD makes His law glorious.
passages.original: יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר׃

passages.text: But this is a people plundered and looted, all trapped in caves or imprisoned in dungeons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say, “Send them back!”
passages.sermon:
This people is plundered and looted.
All of them are trapped in holes.
All of them are hidden in prisons.
They have become plunder.
No one rescues them.
They have become loot.
No one says, "Send them back."
passages.original: וְהוּא֮ עַם־ בָּז֣וּז וְשָׁסוּי֒ הָפֵ֤חַ בַּֽחוּרִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וּבְבָתֵּ֥י כְלָאִ֖ים הָחְבָּ֑אוּ הָי֤וּ לָבַז֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּ֔יל מְשִׁסָּ֖ה וְאֵין־ אֹמֵ֥ר הָשַֽׁב׃

passages.text: Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He asks a question.
Who among you will listen to this?
Who will pay attention?
Who will hear and obey from now on?
passages.original: מִ֥י בָכֶ֖ם יַאֲזִ֣ין זֹ֑את יַקְשִׁ֥ב וְיִשְׁמַ֖ע לְאָחֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They were unwilling to walk in His ways, and they would not obey His law.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel and Jacob.
He has great power and authority.
He gave Jacob to be plundered.
He gave Israel to those who would loot them.
We sinned against the LORD.
We did not want to follow His ways.
We did not obey His law.
passages.original: מִֽי־ נָתַ֨ן לִמְשׁוֹסֶה יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים הֲל֣וֹא יְהוָ֑ה ז֚וּ חָטָ֣אנוּ ל֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־ אָב֤וּ בִדְרָכָיו֙ הָל֔וֹךְ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּתוֹרָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So He poured out on them His furious anger and the fierceness of battle. It enveloped them in flames, but they did not understand; it consumed them, but they did not take it to heart.
passages.sermon:
The LORD became very angry with Israel.
He poured out His furious anger on them.
He sent the fierceness of battle against them.
Flames surrounded them on every side.
They did not understand what was happening.
The fire burned them.
They did not take it to heart.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ חֵמָ֣ה אַפּ֔וֹ וֶעֱז֖וּז מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר־ בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־ יָשִׂ֥ים עַל־ לֵֽב׃פ
